FlashHole detection and placement review

Behavior evidence and boundaries:
- crypto/decrypt: a structured call to a named Threefish decrypt routine.
  The required operation is decryption, not generic algorithm presence.
- crypto/encrypt: a structured GOST encryption call. No CBC mode is inferred;
  the article names GOST/Magma without specifying the mode.
- crypto/key/exchange: ML-KEM/Kyber encapsulation calls, independent of OS.
- crypto/key/import: Go NewEncapsulationKey1024 imports an encoded public key;
  it is not mislabeled as key generation or generic KEM presence.
- evasion/anti-av/syscall: JScript page-protection and copy destinations are
  independently bound to GetProcAddress(..., "MD4Update"). The hostile compound
  requires both within twenty lines. Ordinary crypto and memory copying do not
  establish this specific system-function code-patching abuse.
- well-known/malware/downloader/lpeclient: at least three distinct protocol
  message constants plus ML-KEM and Threefish calls identify the reported
  LPEClient protocol. This is family identity, not generic C2 or payload-flow
  detection. No filename, endpoint, ecosystem or arbitrary marker gates it.

A second placement pass by the alternative-home test reaches the same homes:
algorithm-presence leaves lose the required crypto direction; metadata loses
runtime calls; neutral memory-copy capability loses the resolved system-function
patch target; a generic execution/staging objective lacks the family protocol
identity. This review did not infer privileges, exploit internals or loader
implementation omitted by the report.

Corrections to existing firing traits:
The 1568/0x620 ML-KEM observations describe material-size references rather than
claiming that a public-key size must be ciphertext. The combined observation is
notable because it independently identifies crypto-related material. Generic
KEM routine fragments no longer claim specifically ML-KEM without evidence.

The sample derives a Threefish tweak by XOR; that is not payload decoding.
The following placements preserve matcher patterns and scopes while correcting
names, mappings and references:
- data/encode/xor::xor-bytes-genexpr-literal ->
  data/encoding/xor::python-literal-key-xor-bytes
- data/decode/custom::bytewise-xor-generator-transform ->
  data/arithmetic::literal-key-xor-byte-constructor
  This broad pattern also accepts bytes(size ^ 0xA5), which is arithmetic in a
  constructor rather than proof of a byte stream; its name states that limit.

The neutral XOR moves remove unsupported T1027/B0032/T1140 mappings; criticality
stays notable. All exact consumers were updated. Ancestor selectors for data,
encode, decode, encoding, and their XOR/custom leaves were audited; the only
broad incoming selector was data/encode/xor inside xor-byte-transforms. That
composite now explicitly includes the relocated literal-key generator, keeping
its previous match set. The existing custom-decoder compound references the
relocated arithmetic fact without changing its other evidence.

Directory capacity audit:
Arithmetic was at its 100-rule budget. Auditing its operators found two
redundant Python character-ordinal shift comprehensions: the old
python-chr-ord-shift-generator and python-character-offset-comprehension-reference
expressed the same operation with variable versus numeric offsets and different
whitespace handling. They are consolidated into python-chr-ord-shift-generator,
with the accurate description Character ordinal shift comprehension. No consumer
referenced the retired numeric-offset ID. The consolidated matcher also accepts
spaces around a named offset, a deliberate precision-preserving coverage gain
for the same operation. The ordinal-shift operation remains notable. Arithmetic
stays at 100 rules; there is no capacity exception or artificial directory split.

Fixtures:
Two source reconstructions are registered in testdata/expectations.toml with
min_hostile=2. Thirteen benign/near-miss controls are materialized under cleave's
tests/fixtures/flashhole; their source text is retained in fixture-sources.json
so a clean checkout can reproduce them. check.py tests fifteen cases total,
including read-vs-write, changed target, missing protection/write, documentation,
Python/JavaScript crypto APIs, Go key import, XOR scalar-vs-generator cases, and both ordinal-shift forms with an unshifted
near miss.
The controls forbid hostile findings; only the two deliberate partial patch
examples permit one suspicious finding. This is intentional boundary coverage,
not a blanket benign exclusion.

Full article, primary report, extracted figures/code, indicators, facts and
atomscan evidence are under scratch/threat-feed/4059 (see evidence/notes.txt).
No YARA rules were edited and no precompile is required.
